stemBlocks.value: Evaluate 0.045/0.15 and (ii) give your answer to 2 significant figures.
Think first: Clear the decimals from the divisor before dividing, then round only at the very end.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p009-q06 from workbook page 9.

solutionSteps.instruction: Scale top and bottom by the same power of ten.

contentBlocks.value: The first significant figure is 3; a second one is needed, and it is 0

strategyBlocks.value: Multiply numerator and denominator by 1000 to make both whole numbers, divide, then round the exact result to 2 significant figures.

whyThisWorks.value: Multiplying the numerator and denominator by the same number leaves a fraction's value unchanged, so scaling by 1000 removes the decimals without altering the answer. Significant figures are counted from the first non-zero digit, so in 0.3 the leading zero does not count and a trailing zero must be written to show that two significant figures are being reported.

commonErrors.misconception: Dropping the trailing zero and writing 0.3 when 2 significant figures are demanded.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dropping the trailing zero and writing 0.3 when 2 significant figures are demanded.

commonErrors.misconception: Counting the zero before the decimal point as a significant figure.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Counting the zero before the decimal point as a significant figure.

commonErrors.misconception: Scaling only the denominator, turning 0.045/0.15 into 0.045/150.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Scaling only the denominator, turning 0.045/0.15 into 0.045/150.

examTip.value: Write trailing zeros when a question fixes the number of significant figures — 0.30 and 0.3 are the same value but only one of them answers the question asked.
